clue.text: Extra words from Dad maybe to boy and little girl

parts.note: a dad is one example of a parent
he is the pronoun for a boy
sis is a short, familiar word for a sister

explanation.surface: A father adds a few more words to a note for his son and young daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad maybe' marks an example: a dad is one kind of parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthetical insertion is a remark slipped into a sentence, literally extra words set apart from the rest.

clue.text: Standard component gets shortened

indicators.note: being shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a component is a part of something

explanation.surface: A regular machine part has been cut down in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the accepted normal level, as in 'up to par', so it is a standard.

clue.text: Dish with some meat I artlessly knocked over over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down clue the letters run the other way
some of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A clumsy diner tips over a plate of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ATIAR from 'meAT I ARtlessly'; 'knocked over' turns it round. The second 'over' looks like a doubled word in the printed clue and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or mint.

clue.text: Wicket going down? After that you may hear see such a stir

indicators.note: in a down clue the wicket goes down to the foot of the entry, after the other piece
what you hear is the sound of a word, so a word with the same sound but another spelling is wanted

parts.note: to see in the sense of understand is to know, and knew is its past form
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator reacts to a falling wicket and the fuss that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket reading misleads: a wicket is also a small gate. 'you may hear' makes KNEW (from 'see', understand) give NEW, and 'going down' sends GATE below it. STIR is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a notorious London prison, and stir is slang for a jail, so it is one such stir.

clue.text: Buildings getting very warm? You may want sprinklers around

definitions.text: Buildings getting very warm? You may want sprinklers around

parts.words: Buildings getting very warm? You may want sprinklers around
parts.note: read as buildings on fire needing sprinklers, but it describes glass buildings that are kept heated and where plants are watered

explanation.surface: A fire-safety warning about overheated buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasshouses kept warm for growing plants are heated buildings where watering sprinklers are used.

clue.text: Couple sharing meat and fish

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme couple Jack and his wife shared their meat: he ate no fat, she ate no lean
a small sea fish of the herring family

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme: Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean, so between them they licked the platter clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the nursery-rhyme pair and the name of a small herring-like fish are spelt alike.

clue.text: Going over everybody, short-range shell

indicators.note: one piece going over another covers it, so it surrounds the second piece
short means the word is cut and loses its last letter

parts.note: scope is the range or extent of something
everybody means all

explanation.surface: A short-range shell is fired over the heads of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short-range shell' reads as artillery, but 'shell' alone is the definition; 'short' cuts the last letter from the range word and 'Going over' wraps it round the everybody word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve mollusc, and its fan-shaped shell is also called a scallop.

clue.text: Dry in a very short time

definitions.meaning: ... describes wine that is dry, not sweet
... is short for second, as in 'wait a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Sec is the wine word for dry and also the clipped form of a second, a moment.

clue.text: Mad pets on the loose — little boy rushed in panic

indicators.note: things on the loose are free and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: Crazed pets escape and a small boy flees in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To stampede is to rush in a frightened mass, as animals do when panicked.

clue.text: Bring together prisoners and make known mischief-maker

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
to tell is to make something known
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Gathering inmates together and exposing the troublemaker among them.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE is the Greek goddess of mischief and folly.
explanation.definitionFit: To constellate is to cluster or gather together, like stars in a group.

clue.text: Result of downfall of old Prince, one yielding to rebel leader

indicators.note: one thing yielding to another gives up its place to it, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: Rainier III was a former Prince of Monaco
the Roman numeral for one
Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A deposed prince gives way to a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The political 'downfall' is a fall of rain. WAT Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that falls from the sky collects after a downpour, so it is what a downfall leaves.

clue.text: A by-election success a second time

parts.note: a party winning a by-election seat records a gain

explanation.surface: A party wins a by-election for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more is doing it a second time, which is the plain sense of again.

clue.text: Show of courage from supporter opposing fuss

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
v, short for versus, means against
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A fan shows nerve by objecting to a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan; it is an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold display of courage, often more show than substance.

clue.text: Amazing person entertaining American playwright

indicators.note: one piece entertaining another holds it as a guest, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
Thornton Wilder wrote the play Our Town

explanation.surface: A remarkable person plays host to a US dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bewildering is confusing in a way that leaves one astonished, the adjectival sense of amazing.

clue.text: Tree little child planted to give a border cover

indicators.note: the child piece covers the other on both sides, surrounding it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a lip is a rim or border

explanation.surface: A small child plants a tree to provide cover for a garden border.
explanation.definitionFit: The talipot is a tall Asian fan palm, a tree with huge leaves.

clue.text: This general's said to be a cruel person

indicators.note: said means spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory or cruel person

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain general was a savage man.
explanation.walkthrough: James WOLFE was the British general who took Quebec in 1759.
explanation.definitionFit: James Wolfe was the British general who won at Quebec, so he is the general meant.

clue.text: An old drunk, loud fellow upset sleep

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, the letters running backwards

parts.note: a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A drunken old man and a noisy chap disturb someone's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges AN OLD to LANDO; 'upset' turns DON to NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of Nod is the jocular name for the state of sleep, from nodding off.

clue.text: Put one's foot down in a quiet sort of way?

definitions.text: Put one's foot down in a quiet sort of way?

parts.words: Put one's foot down in a quiet sort of way?
parts.note: looks like asserting oneself gently, but literally means pressing the piano pedal that makes playing quieter

explanation.surface: A question about laying down the law gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down or tone something down, from the piano's quietening pedal.

clue.text: She looks fantastic in love affairs — it's the special tights

indicators.note: one piece set in another sits inside it

parts.note: flings are brief love affairs

indicators.note: looking fantastic suggests an altered, imaginative arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A woman looks stunning in her romances, thanks to her tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks fantastic' turns SHE into ESH, which goes 'in' FLINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshings are flesh-coloured tights worn by performers to suggest bare skin.

clue.text: Eat no slug — horrible thing to devour!

indicators.note: horrible suggests something grotesquely twisted, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner refuses to eat a slug, a dreadful thing to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, a shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: O to be in Athens!

parts.note: reads like a wistful cry to visit Greece, but asks what the letter O is called in Greek

explanation.surface: A homesick sigh for the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Browning's 'Oh, to be in England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek alphabet's short o, the letter O as written in Athens.

clue.text: Member of old empire with a fabulous princess

parts.note: the Medes were people of an ancient empire in Persia

explanation.surface: An ancient imperial subject keeps company with a legendary princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea was the princess of Colchis in Greek myth, and fabulous here means legendary.

clue.text: Butter up man given highest ranking in assessment

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts
the king is the most important chess man

explanation.surface: Flattering the person at the top of the rankings in a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter up' looks like flatter; 'Butter' is something that butts, a RAM, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking is the grading of work, an act of assessment by a teacher.

clue.text: Salacious stuff girl's found in holy books? The opposite!

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it
the opposite reverses the stated arrangement, so the books go inside the girl

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: A girl's racy reading is found among religious texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite!' flips 'found in': taken literally the girl would sit in the books, but it is the books that go inside the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually explicit writing or art, salacious material.

clue.text: Capital account starts to concern responsible auditor

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An auditor checks the capital account.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: In this place get right of pasture

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: here means in this place
to bag is to get or secure

explanation.surface: Someone demands grazing rights on this land.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is the legal right to graze animals on another's land, as well as pasture itself.

clue.text: Look for a funny person, entertaining, ace

indicators.note: one piece entertaining another holds it inside

parts.note: a wit is an amusing person
a is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Waiting for a comedian who entertains brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To await is to wait for or look out for something expected.

clue.text: Archers know about this, showing little hesitation at The Bull?

indicators.note: one piece at another is placed after it

parts.note: the Bull is a typical pub name, and a pub is an inn
er is a small sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Fans of the radio soap The Archers know that someone hesitates at the village pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap with a pub called The Bull, but archers here are bowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of an archery target just outside the bull, familiar to every archer.

clue.text: One's usually put up with one's rivals

definitions.text: One's usually put up with one's rivals

parts.words: One's usually put up with one's rivals
parts.note: sounds like tolerating competitors, but describes someone nominated, or put up, for election alongside opponents

explanation.surface: A remark about having to tolerate competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is nominated, or put up, to stand for election against others.

clue.text: Aim to post first letter off

indicators.note: with the first letter off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: The goal is to mail the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or goal, as in 'to that end'.

clue.text: Tribe's carefree adventure

definitions.meaning: One of the twelve tribes of Israel
a ..., as in 'on the ...', is a jaunt or roving trip

explanation.definitionFit: Gad names an Israelite tribe and, as a noun, a carefree roaming trip.

clue.text: With impaired vision, the reading's tricky

indicators.note: tricky suggests a puzzle to be worked out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short-sighted person finds reading hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'reading's' is 'reading is', so its S counts in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nearsighted means seeing near things clearly but distant ones blurred, a form of impaired vision.
